# EasyCalculator

![EasyCalculator logo](reference/figures/logo.png)

### 🇮🇳 Simple, transparent financial calculators for India — built in R

A growing toolbox of financial calculators — **income tax** today, with
**GST** and **loan** calculators on the way — each usable for one person
or a whole portfolio in a single line of R.

site](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pkgdown-blue?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://poduval.github.io/EasyCalculator/)

> EasyCalculator is currently **under active review**, and significant
> improvements are being worked on. 🛠️ In the meantime you may run into
> bugs, rough edges or results that don’t match the official rules.
> **Please pardon any problems you find at this stage** 🙏 — and if you
> spot one, [opening an
> issue](https://github.com/Poduval/EasyCalculator/issues) would be a
> big help. Thank you for your patience and support! 💙

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✨ Why EasyCalculator?

|  | Feature | What you get |
|----|----|----|
| 🧰 | **Many calculators, one package** | Income tax today; GST and loan calculators planned — all sharing one consistent style. |
| ⚡ | **One-liner** | `tax_payable(1150000)` — done. |
| 👥 | **Bulk-ready** | Pass a data frame of hundreds of people and get one tidy result back. |
| 📊 | **Data-driven rules** | Rates, slabs and limits live in plain data tables, not buried in code — easy to audit and update. |
| 🔍 | **Transparent output** | A step-by-step breakdown, not just a final number. |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🧰 Calculators

| Calculator | Function | Status |
|----|----|:--:|
| 🧮 Income tax (old vs new regime) | [`tax_payable()`](https://poduval.github.io/EasyCalculator/reference/tax_payable.md) | ✅ Available |
| 🧾 GST | `gst_calculator()` | 🗓️ Planned |
| 🏦 Loan scheduler | `loan_schedular()` | 🗓️ Planned |

Every calculator is documented on the [reference
page](https://poduval.github.io/EasyCalculator/reference/index.html) of
the package website.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📦 Installation

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("Poduval/EasyCalculator")
```

``` r

library(EasyCalculator)
```

> 💡 Requires **R ≥ 4.1.0** and the
> [`plyr`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=plyr) package.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🚀 Quick start

The examples below use the income tax calculator, the first one
available.

### 👤 A single taxpayer

``` r

# New regime (default), financial year 2024
tax_payable(1150000)

# Old regime
tax_payable(1150000, tax_regime = "old")
```

### 👥 Many taxpayers at once

``` r

people <- data.frame(
  id            = c(1, 2, 3),
  annual_income = c(1400000, 2000000, 3000000)
)

tax_payable(people)
```

### 💼 With investment deductions (old regime)

``` r

person <- data.frame(
  id            = 1,
  annual_income = 1500000,
  tax_regime    = "old",
  declared_NPS  = 50000,
  declared_80C  = 150000,
  declared_80D  = 25000
)

tax_payable(person)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🧮 Tax calculator

[`tax_payable()`](https://poduval.github.io/EasyCalculator/reference/tax_payable.md)
computes Indian income tax under the **Old** and **New** regimes. It
handles the standard deduction, investment deductions (NPS, 80C, 80D,
24B, 80TTA — capped at statutory limits, old regime), Section 87A rebate
and 4% surcharge/cess.

### 🔧 Inputs

| Column | Required | Description |
|----|:--:|----|
| `id` | ✅ | Identifier for each taxpayer |
| `annual_income` | ✅ | Gross annual income (₹) |
| `financial_year` | ➖ | Defaults to `2024` |
| `tax_regime` | ➖ | `"new"` (default) or `"old"` |
| `declared_NPS` `declared_80C` `declared_80D` `declared_24B` `declared_80TTA` | ➖ | Declared investments / deductions (old regime only) |

### 📤 Output

A data frame of class `ITR` with a readable
[`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) method and full detail
underneath:

| Column                        | Meaning                                  |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| 💰 `annual_income`            | Income you supplied                      |
| 🧾 `taxable_amount`           | Income after exemptions and deductions   |
| 📉 `rebate_under_investments` | Deductions allowed after applying limits |
| 🧮 `tax_from_income_slab`     | Tax computed from the slabs              |
| 🎁 `rebate_under_87A`         | Section 87A rebate applied               |
| 🏛️ `tax_surcharge`            | 4% surcharge / cess                      |
| ✅ `tax_value`                | The tax you owe                          |

### 📈 FY 2024 slabs

[TABLE]

### 🏷️ Deduction limits (old regime, FY 2024)

|   Section    | Covers                   | Limit (₹) |
|:------------:|--------------------------|----------:|
|  🏦 **NPS**  | National Pension Scheme  |    50,000 |
|  🛡️ **80C**  | Tax-saving investments   |  1,50,000 |
|  ⚕️ **80D**  | Medical insurance        |  1,50,000 |
|  🏠 **24B**  | Home-loan interest       |  2,00,000 |
| 💳 **80TTA** | Savings-account interest |    10,000 |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ⚙️ How it works

``` mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["👤 Income &<br/>declarations"] --> B["🧾 Basic exemption<br/>+ standard deduction"]
    B --> C["💼 Investment deductions<br/>(capped, old regime)"]
    C --> D["📊 Slab tax"]
    D --> E["🎁 Section 87A<br/>rebate"]
    E --> F["🏛️ 4% surcharge<br/>/ cess"]
    F --> G["✅ Tax payable"]

    classDef input fill:#E3F2FD,stroke:#1E88E5,color:#0D47A1;
    classDef step fill:#FFF8E1,stroke:#FB8C00,color:#E65100;
    classDef out fill:#E8F5E9,stroke:#43A047,color:#1B5E20;
    class A input;
    class B,C,D,E,F step;
    class G out;
```

The tax calculator is deliberately small and layered (new calculators
follow the same generic → method → data-table pattern):

``` mermaid
flowchart TB
    G["tax_payable(x, ...)<br/><i>S3 generic</i>"] --> N["tax_payable.default<br/><i>numeric vector</i>"]
    G --> DF["tax_payable.data.frame<br/><i>the engine</i>"]
    N -->|builds a data frame| DF
    DF --> T[("📚 data.* tables<br/>slabs · rebates · limits")]
    DF --> P["print.ITR<br/><i>friendly summary</i>"]
```

> 🧠 **Rules are data, not code.** Every slab, exemption and limit is
> stored in a table keyed by `tax_regime` and `financial_year`, so
> supporting a new Budget is mostly a matter of adding rows.

## 🗺️ Roadmap

``` mermaid
timeline
    title EasyCalculator journey
    section Released
        v0.0.1 : 🧮 Income tax calculator
    section Planned
        Calculators : 🧾 GST calculator : 🏦 Loan scheduler
        Insights : 📊 summary & plot methods : 📘 Vignettes & cheat sheet
        Apps : 🖥️ Embedded Shiny app : 🔗 Links to official references
```

🧮 Income tax calculator —
[`tax_payable()`](https://poduval.github.io/EasyCalculator/reference/tax_payable.md)

🧾 GST calculator — `gst_calculator()`

🏦 Loan scheduler — `loan_schedular()`

📊 [`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) methods

📘 Vignettes (examples and concepts) and a cheat sheet

🖥️ Embedded Shiny app

📅 Additional financial years

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ⚠️ Good to know

- 📅 For the tax calculator, only **FY 2024** rules are included today.
  Unknown years fall back to 2024 in data-frame input.
- 🚧 The package is **under review**; expect changes and improvements,
  and please report any issues you find.
- 🧑‍⚖️ This package is an aid for estimation and learning — **not**
  professional tax advice. Always verify against the official Income Tax
  Department rules or consult a qualified tax professional.

    `devtools::document()`)
3.  ✅ Run `devtools::check()`
4.  📬 Open a pull request
